card.title: I Know Your Tells
card.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tapped your cup three times. You're about to ask for money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm waiting for the tea to cool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the story you used before the bicycle loan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Actually, I brought the bicycle money back. I've counted it twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twice? That's not checking the amount; that's giving me time to refuse it. Keep it; I'll make your usual celebratory tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 diagnoses the tapping, A3 cites the bicycle-loan habit, and A5 explains double counting as a familiar strategy for eliciting refusal.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cooling account informs A3's pattern claim; B4's counted repayment supplies the exact action A5 diagnoses and responds to.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer plausible alternatives to A's reading, including actually bringing the debt back.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's counting time to infer an unstated wish, waive repayment, and prepare the familiar celebration.

specificity.evidence: A1-B4 establish tea, an earlier bicycle loan and its offered repayment.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's giving-me-time reading ties the waiver to B4's double count without another late anecdote.
